content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (T4C), preferred-level cure.**

- **Responsive locations reviewed:** 18.1 (p0228, 25-year Initial Period; exit only at/after its end on one year's notice), 18.2 (p0229, mid-term termination only by unanimous agreement / 90% Management Committee vote), 18.4 (p0231, p0233, no capital-cost credit on withdrawal), 18.5–18.7 (p0232, p0234, p0235), plus Paragraph 23 default/capacity-reclamation (p0255–p0257, cause-based, not convenience).
- **Classification:** No Customer convenience right exists in a 25-year term — walk-away territory, failing fallback (no 60–90 day right, no capped early-termination fee). The counterparty side already satisfies the preferred element: no Party may exit during the Initial Period, and 18.1 requires one year's notice thereafter, so that element was mapped as already_met with a verbatim quote rather than re-drafted.
- **Cure:** a single insert of new Subparagraph 18.8 giving Teleglobe alone a convenience exit on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts. It is expressed as "in addition to Subparagraph 18.1" to avoid a broad notwithstanding override, gives the other Parties no new rights, and leaves the 18.1-specific capital-cost forfeiture untouched.
